/*
 * jcsample.c
 *
 * This file was part of the Independent JPEG Group's software:
 * Copyright (C) 1991-1996, Thomas G. Lane.
 * libjpeg-turbo Modifications:
 * Copyright 2009 Pierre Ossman <ossman@cendio.se> for Cendio AB
 * Copyright (C) 2014, MIPS Technologies, Inc., California.
 * Copyright (C) 2015, 2019, D. R. Commander.
 * For conditions of distribution and use, see the accompanying README.ijg
 * file.
 *
 * This file contains downsampling routines.
 *
 * Downsampling input data is counted in "row groups".  A row group
 * is defined to be max_v_samp_factor pixel rows of each component,
 * from which the downsampler produces v_samp_factor sample rows.
 * A single row group is processed in each call to the downsampler module.
 *
 * The downsampler is responsible for edge-expansion of its output data
 * to fill an integral number of DCT blocks horizontally.  The source buffer
 * may be modified if it is helpful for this purpose (the source buffer is
 * allocated wide enough to correspond to the desired output width).
 * The caller (the prep controller) is responsible for vertical padding.
 *
 * The downsampler may request "context rows" by setting need_context_rows
 * during startup.  In this case, the input arrays will contain at least
 * one row group's worth of pixels above and below the passed-in data;
 * the caller will create dummy rows at image top and bottom by replicating
 * the first or last real pixel row.
 *
 * An excellent reference for image resampling is
 *   Digital Image Warping, George Wolberg, 1990.
 *   Pub. by IEEE Computer Society Press, Los Alamitos, CA. ISBN 0-8186-8944-7.
 *
 * The downsampling algorithm used here is a simple average of the source
 * pixels covered by the output pixel.  The hi-falutin sampling literature
 * refers to this as a "box filter".  In general the characteristics of a box
 * filter are not very good, but for the specific cases we normally use (1:1
 * and 2:1 ratios) the box is equivalent to a "triangle filter" which is not
 * nearly so bad.  If you intend to use other sampling ratios, you'd be well
 * advised to improve this code.
 *
 * A simple input-smoothing capability is provided.  This is mainly intended
 * for cleaning up color-dithered GIF input files (if you find it inadequate,
 * we suggest using an external filtering program such as pnmconvol).  When
 * enabled, each input pixel P is replaced by a weighted sum of itself and its
 * eight neighbors.  P's weight is 1-8*SF and each neighbor's weight is SF,
 * where SF = (smoothing_factor / 1024).
 * Currently, smoothing is only supported for 2h2v sampling factors.
 */

Sources:
third_party/deps/jpeg/jcstest.c

/*
 * jdmerge.c
 *
 * This file was part of the Independent JPEG Group's software:
 * Copyright (C) 1994-1996, Thomas G. Lane.
 * libjpeg-turbo Modifications:
 * Copyright 2009 Pierre Ossman <ossman@cendio.se> for Cendio AB
 * Copyright (C) 2009, 2011, 2014-2015, 2020, D. R. Commander.
 * Copyright (C) 2013, Linaro Limited.
 * For conditions of distribution and use, see the accompanying README.ijg
 * file.
 *
 * This file contains code for merged upsampling/color conversion.
 *
 * This file combines functions from jdsample.c and jdcolor.c;
 * read those files first to understand what's going on.
 *
 * When the chroma components are to be upsampled by simple replication
 * (ie, box filtering), we can save some work in color conversion by
 * calculating all the output pixels corresponding to a pair of chroma
 * samples at one time.  In the conversion equations
 *      R = Y           + K1 * Cr
 *      G = Y + K2 * Cb + K3 * Cr
 *      B = Y + K4 * Cb
 * only the Y term varies among the group of pixels corresponding to a pair
 * of chroma samples, so the rest of the terms can be calculated just once.
 * At typical sampling ratios, this eliminates half or three-quarters of the
 * multiplications needed for color conversion.
 *
 * This file currently provides implementations for the following cases:
 *      YCbCr => RGB color conversion only.
 *      Sampling ratios of 2h1v or 2h2v.
 *      No scaling needed at upsample time.
 *      Corner-aligned (non-CCIR601) sampling alignment.
 * Other special cases could be added, but in most applications these are
 * the only common cases.  (For uncommon cases we fall back on the more
 * general code in jdsample.c and jdcolor.c.)
 */

Sources:
third_party/deps/jpeg/jdmerge.h

/*
 * jdmerge.h

 * This file was part of the Independent JPEG Group's software:
 * Copyright (C) 1994-1996, Thomas G. Lane.

/*
 * jdsample.c
 *
 * This file was part of the Independent JPEG Group's software:
 * Copyright (C) 1991-1996, Thomas G. Lane.
 * libjpeg-turbo Modifications:
 * Copyright 2009 Pierre Ossman <ossman@cendio.se> for Cendio AB
 * Copyright (C) 2010, 2015-2016, D. R. Commander.
 * Copyright (C) 2014, MIPS Technologies, Inc., California.
 * Copyright (C) 2015, Google, Inc.
 * Copyright (C) 2019-2020, Arm Limited.
 * For conditions of distribution and use, see the accompanying README.ijg
 * file.
 *
 * This file contains upsampling routines.
 *
 * Upsampling input data is counted in "row groups".  A row group
 * is defined to be (v_samp_factor * DCT_scaled_size / min_DCT_scaled_size)
 * sample rows of each component.  Upsampling will normally produce
 * max_v_samp_factor pixel rows from each row group (but this could vary
 * if the upsampler is applying a scale factor of its own).
 *
 * An excellent reference for image resampling is
 *   Digital Image Warping, George Wolberg, 1990.
 *   Pub. by IEEE Computer Society Press, Los Alamitos, CA. ISBN 0-8186-8944-7.
 */

Sources:

third_party/deps/jpeg/jfdctflt.c

/*
 * jfdctflt.c
 *
 * Copyright (C) 1994-1996, Thomas G. Lane.
 * This file is part of the Independent JPEG Group's software.
 * For conditions of distribution and use, see the accompanying README.ijg
 * file.
 *
 * This file contains a floating-point implementation of the
 * forward DCT (Discrete Cosine Transform).
 *
 * This implementation should be more accurate than either of the integer
 * DCT implementations.  However, it may not give the same results on all
 * machines because of differences in roundoff behavior.  Speed will depend
 * on the hardware's floating point capacity.
 *
 * A 2-D DCT can be done by 1-D DCT on each row followed by 1-D DCT
 * on each column.  Direct algorithms are also available, but they are
 * much more complex and seem not to be any faster when reduced to code.
 *
 * This implementation is based on Arai, Agui, and Nakajima's algorithm for
 * scaled DCT.  Their original paper (Trans. IEICE E-71(11):1095) is in
 * Japanese, but the algorithm is described in the Pennebaker & Mitchell
 * JPEG textbook (see REFERENCES section in file README.ijg).  The following
 * code is based directly on figure 4-8 in P&M.
 * While an 8-point DCT cannot be done in less than 11 multiplies, it is
 * possible to arrange the computation so that many of the multiplies are
 * simple scalings of the final outputs.  These multiplies can then be
 * folded into the multiplications or divisions by the JPEG quantization
 * table entries.  The AA&N method leaves only 5 multiplies and 29 adds
 * to be done in the DCT itself.
 * The primary disadvantage of this method is that with a fixed-point
 * implementation, accuracy is lost due to imprecise representation of the
 * scaled quantization values.  However, that problem does not arise if
 * we use floating point arithmetic.
 */

 * libjpeg-turbo Modifications:
 * Copyright (C) 2015, D. R. Commander.

 * forward DCT (Discrete Cosine Transform).
 *
 * A 2-D DCT can be done by 1-D DCT on each row followed by 1-D DCT
 * on each column.  Direct algorithms are also available, but they are
 * much more complex and seem not to be any faster when reduced to code.
 *
 * This implementation is based on Arai, Agui, and Nakajima's algorithm for
 * scaled DCT.  Their original paper (Trans. IEICE E-71(11):1095) is in
 * Japanese, but the algorithm is described in the Pennebaker & Mitchell
 * JPEG textbook (see REFERENCES section in file README.ijg).  The following
 * code is based directly on figure 4-8 in P&M.
 * While an 8-point DCT cannot be done in less than 11 multiplies, it is
 * possible to arrange the computation so that many of the multiplies are
 * simple scalings of the final outputs.  These multiplies can then be
 * folded into the multiplications or divisions by the JPEG quantization
 * table entries.  The AA&N method leaves only 5 multiplies and 29 adds
 * to be done in the DCT itself.
 * The primary disadvantage of this method is that with fixed-point math,
 * accuracy is lost due to imprecise representation of the scaled
 * quantization values.  The smaller the quantization table entry, the less
 * precise the scaled value, so this implementation does worse with high-
 * quality-setting files than with low-quality ones.
 */

/*
 * jfdctint.c
 *
 * This file was part of the Independent JPEG Group's software:
 * Copyright (C) 1991-1996, Thomas G. Lane.
 * libjpeg-turbo Modifications:
 * Copyright (C) 2015, 2020, D. R. Commander.
 * For conditions of distribution and use, see the accompanying README.ijg
 * file.
 *
 * This file contains a slower but more accurate integer implementation of the
 * forward DCT (Discrete Cosine Transform).
 *
 * A 2-D DCT can be done by 1-D DCT on each row followed by 1-D DCT
 * on each column.  Direct algorithms are also available, but they are
 * much more complex and seem not to be any faster when reduced to code.
 *
 * This implementation is based on an algorithm described in
 *   C. Loeffler, A. Ligtenberg and G. Moschytz, "Practical Fast 1-D DCT
 *   Algorithms with 11 Multiplications", Proc. Int'l. Conf. on Acoustics,
 *   Speech, and Signal Processing 1989 (ICASSP '89), pp. 988-991.
 * The primary algorithm described there uses 11 multiplies and 29 adds.
 * We use their alternate method with 12 multiplies and 32 adds.
 * The advantage of this method is that no data path contains more than one
 * multiplication; this allows a very simple and accurate implementation in
 * scaled fixed-point arithmetic, with a minimal number of shifts.
 */

 * complex and seem not to be any faster when reduced to code.

 * Japanese, but the algorithm is described in the Pennebaker & Mitchell
 * JPEG textbook (see REFERENCES section in file README.ijg).  The following
 * code is based directly on figure 4-8 in P&M.
 * While an 8-point DCT cannot be done in less than 11 multiplies, it is
 * possible to arrange the computation so that many of the multiplies are
 * simple scalings of the final outputs.  These multiplies can then be
 * folded into the multiplications or divisions by the JPEG quantization
 * table entries.  The AA&N method leaves only 5 multiplies and 29 adds
 * to be done in the DCT itself.
 * The primary disadvantage of this method is that with a fixed-point
 * implementation, accuracy is lost due to imprecise representation of the
 * scaled quantization values.  However, that problem does not arise if
 * we use floating point arithmetic.
 */

Sources:
third_party/deps/jpeg/jidctint.c

/*
 * jidctint.c
 *
 * This file was part of the Independent JPEG Group's software:
 * Copyright (C) 1991-1998, Thomas G. Lane.
 * Modification developed 2002-2018 by Guido Vollbeding.
 * libjpeg-turbo Modifications:
 * Copyright (C) 2015, 2020, D. R. Commander.
 * For conditions of distribution and use, see the accompanying README.ijg
 * file.
 *
 * This file contains a slower but more accurate integer implementation of the
 * inverse DCT (Discrete Cosine Transform).  In the IJG code, this routine
 * must also perform dequantization of the input coefficients.
 *
 * A 2-D IDCT can be done by 1-D IDCT on each column followed by 1-D IDCT
 * on each row (or vice versa, but it's more convenient to emit a row at
 * a time).  Direct algorithms are also available, but they are much more
 * complex and seem not to be any faster when reduced to code.
 *
 * This implementation is based on an algorithm described in
 *   C. Loeffler, A. Ligtenberg and G. Moschytz, "Practical Fast 1-D DCT
 *   Algorithms with 11 Multiplications", Proc. Int'l. Conf. on Acoustics,
 *   Speech, and Signal Processing 1989 (ICASSP '89), pp. 988-991.
 * The primary algorithm described there uses 11 multiplies and 29 adds.
 * We use their alternate method with 12 multiplies and 32 adds.
 * The advantage of this method is that no data path contains more than one
 * multiplication; this allows a very simple and accurate implementation in
 * scaled fixed-point arithmetic, with a minimal number of shifts.
 *
 * We also provide IDCT routines with various output sample block sizes for
 * direct resolution reduction or enlargement without additional resampling:
 * NxN (N=1...16) pixels for one 8x8 input DCT block.
 *
 * For N<8 we simply take the corresponding low-frequency coefficients of
 * the 8x8 input DCT block and apply an NxN point IDCT on the sub-block
 * to yield the downscaled outputs.
 * This can be seen as direct low-pass downsampling from the DCT domain
 * point of view rather than the usual spatial domain point of view,
 * yielding significant computational savings and results at least
 * as good as common bilinear (averaging) spatial downsampling.
 *
 * For N>8 we apply a partial NxN IDCT on the 8 input coefficients as
 * lower frequencies and higher frequencies assumed to be zero.
 * It turns out that the computational effort is similar to the 8x8 IDCT
 * regarding the output size.
 * Furthermore, the scaling and descaling is the same for all IDCT sizes.
 *
 * CAUTION: We rely on the FIX() macro except for the N=1,2,4,8 cases
 * since there would be too many additional constants to pre-calculate.
 */

Sources:
third_party/deps/jpeg/jidctred.c

/*
 * jidctred.c
 *
 * This file was part of the Independent JPEG Group's software:
 * Copyright (C) 1994-1998, Thomas G. Lane.
 * libjpeg-turbo Modifications:
 * Copyright (C) 2015, D. R. Commander.
 * For conditions of distribution and use, see the accompanying README.ijg
 * file.
 *
 * This file contains inverse-DCT routines that produce reduced-size output:
 * either 4x4, 2x2, or 1x1 pixels from an 8x8 DCT block.
 *
 * The implementation is based on the Loeffler, Ligtenberg and Moschytz (LL&M)
 * algorithm used in jidctint.c.  We simply replace each 8-to-8 1-D IDCT step
 * with an 8-to-4 step that produces the four averages of two adjacent outputs
 * (or an 8-to-2 step producing two averages of four outputs, for 2x2 output).
 * These steps were derived by computing the corresponding values at the end
 * of the normal LL&M code, then simplifying as much as possible.
 *
 * 1x1 is trivial: just take the DC coefficient divided by 8.
 *
 * See jidctint.c for additional comments.
 */

/*
 * jmemmgr.c
 *
 * This file was part of the Independent JPEG Group's software:
 * Copyright (C) 1991-1997, Thomas G. Lane.
 * libjpeg-turbo Modifications:
 * Copyright (C) 2016, 2021-2022, D. R. Commander.
 * For conditions of distribution and use, see the accompanying README.ijg
 * file.
 *
 * This file contains the JPEG system-independent memory management
 * routines.  This code is usable across a wide variety of machines; most
 * of the system dependencies have been isolated in a separate file.
 * The major functions provided here are:
 *   * pool-based allocation and freeing of memory;
 *   * policy decisions about how to divide available memory among the
 *     virtual arrays;
 *   * control logic for swapping virtual arrays between main memory and
 *     backing storage.
 * The separate system-dependent file provides the actual backing-storage
 * access code, and it contains the policy decision about how much total
 * main memory to use.
 * This file is system-dependent in the sense that some of its functions
 * are unnecessary in some systems.  For example, if there is enough virtual
 * memory so that backing storage will never be used, much of the virtual
 * array control logic could be removed.  (Of course, if you have that much
 * memory then you shouldn't care about a little bit of unused code...)
 */

third_party/deps/jpeg/rdcolmap.c

/*
 * rdcolmap.c
 *
 * Copyright (C) 1994-1996, Thomas G. Lane.
 * This file is part of the Independent JPEG Group's software.
 * For conditions of distribution and use, see the accompanying README.ijg
 * file.
 *
 * This file implements djpeg's "-map file" switch.  It reads a source image
 * and constructs a colormap to be supplied to the JPEG decompressor.
 *
 * Currently, these file formats are supported for the map file:
 *   GIF: the contents of the GIF's global colormap are used.
 *   PPM (either text or raw flavor): the entire file is read and
 *      each unique pixel value is entered in the map.
 * Note that reading a large PPM file will be horrendously slow.
 * Typically, a PPM-format map file should contain just one pixel
 * of each desired color.  Such a file can be extracted from an
 * ordinary image PPM file with ppmtomap(1).
 *
 * Rescaling a PPM that has a maxval unequal to MAXJSAMPLE is not

/* ==========================================================================
 * siphash.h - SipHash-2-4 in a single header file
 * --------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Derived by William Ahern from the reference implementation[1] published[2]
 * by Jean-Philippe Aumasson and Daniel J. Berstein.
 * Minimal changes by Sebastian Pipping and Victor Stinner on top, see below.
 * Licensed under the CC0 Public Domain Dedication license.
 *
 * 1. https://www.131002.net/siphash/siphash24.c
 * 2. https://www.131002.net/siphash/
 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: CC0-1.0
 * --------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * HISTORY:
 *
 * 2020-10-03  (Sebastian Pipping)
 *   - Drop support for Visual Studio 9.0/2008 and earlier
 *
 * 2019-08-03  (Sebastian Pipping)
 *   - Mark part of sip24_valid as to be excluded from clang-format
 *   - Re-format code using clang-format 9
 *
 * 2018-07-08  (Anton Maklakov)
 *   - Add "fall through" markers for GCC's -Wimplicit-fallthrough
 *
 * 2017-11-03  (Sebastian Pipping)
 *   - Hide sip_tobin and sip_binof unless SIPHASH_TOBIN macro is defined
 *
 * 2017-07-25  (Vadim Zeitlin)
 *   - Fix use of SIPHASH_MAIN macro
 *
 * 2017-07-05  (Sebastian Pipping)
 *   - Use _SIP_ULL macro to not require a C++11 compiler if compiled as C++
 *   - Add const qualifiers at two places
 *   - Ensure <=80 characters line length (assuming tab width 4)
 *
 * 2017-06-23  (Victor Stinner)
 *   - Address Win64 compile warnings
 *
 * 2017-06-18  (Sebastian Pipping)
 *   - Clarify license note in the header
 *   - Address C89 issues:
 *     - Stop using inline keyword (and let compiler decide)
 *     - Replace _Bool by int
 *     - Turn macro siphash24 into a function
 *     - Address invalid conversion (void pointer) by explicit cast
 *   - Address lack of stdint.h for Visual Studio 2003 to 2008
 *   - Always expose sip24_valid (for self-tests)
 *
 * 2012-11-04 - Born.  (William Ahern)
 * --------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * USAGE:
 *
 * SipHash-2-4 takes as input two 64-bit words as the key, some number of
 * message bytes, and outputs a 64-bit word as the message digest. This
 * implementation employs two data structures: a struct sipkey for
 * representing the key, and a struct siphash for representing the hash
 * state.
 *
 * For converting a 16-byte unsigned char array to a key, use either the
 * macro sip_keyof or the routine sip_tokey. The former instantiates a
 * compound literal key, while the latter requires a key object as a
 * parameter.
 *
 * 	unsigned char secret[16];
 * 	arc4random_buf(secret, sizeof secret);
 * 	struct sipkey *key = sip_keyof(secret);
 *
 * For hashing a message, use either the convenience macro siphash24 or the
 * routines sip24_init, sip24_update, and sip24_final.
 *
 * 	struct siphash state;
 * 	void *msg;
 * 	size_t len;
 * 	uint64_t hash;
 *
 * 	sip24_init(&state, key);
 * 	sip24_update(&state, msg, len);
 * 	hash = sip24_final(&state);
 *
 * or
 *
 * 	hash = siphash24(msg, len, key);
 *
 * To convert the 64-bit hash value to a canonical 8-byte little-endian
 * binary representation, use either the macro sip_binof or the routine
 * sip_tobin. The former instantiates and returns a compound literal array,
 * while the latter requires an array object as a parameter.
 * --------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * NOTES:
 *
 * o Neither sip_keyof, sip_binof, nor siphash24 will work with compilers
 *   lacking compound literal support. Instead, you must use the lower-level
 *   interfaces which take as parameters the temporary state objects.
 *
 * o Uppercase macros may evaluate parameters more than once. Lowercase
 *   macros should not exhibit any such side effects.
 * ==========================================================================
 */

======================================================================
third_party/licenses/libstdc++6-Debian-copyright.txt
======================================================================

This is the Debian GNU/Linux prepackaged version of the GNU compiler
collection, containing Ada, C, C++, D, Fortran 95, Go, Objective-C,
Objective-C++, and Modula-2 compilers, documentation, and support
libraries.  In addition, Debian provides the gm2 compiler, either in
the same source package, or built from a separate same source package.
Packaging is done by the Debian GCC Maintainers
<debian-gcc@lists.debian.org>, with sources obtained from:

  ftp://gcc.gnu.org/pub/gcc/releases/  (for full releases)
  svn://gcc.gnu.org/svn/gcc/           (for prereleases)
  ftp://sourceware.org/pub/newlib/     (for newlib)
  git://git.savannah.gnu.org/gm2.git   (for Modula-2)

The current gcc-14 source package is taken from the git gcc-14-branch.

Changes: See changelog.Debian.gz

Debian splits the GNU Compiler Collection into packages for each language,
library, and documentation as follows:

Language       Compiler package  Library package    Documentation
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Ada            gnat-14          libgnat-14          gnat-14-doc
C              gcc-14                              gcc-14-doc
C++            g++-14           libstdc++6         libstdc++6-14-doc
D              gdc-14
Fortran 95     gfortran-14      libgfortran5       gfortran-14-doc
Go             gccgo-14         libgo0
Objective C    gobjc-14         libobjc4
Objective C++  gobjc++-14
Modula-2       gm2-14           libgm2
Rust           gccrs-14

For some language run-time libraries, Debian provides source files,
development files, debugging symbols and libraries containing position-
independent code in separate packages:

Language  Sources      Development   Debugging            Position-Independent
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
C++                                  libstdc++6-14-dbg  libstdc++6-14-pic
D         libphobos-14-dev

Additional packages include:

All languages:
libgcc1, libgcc2, libgcc4       GCC intrinsics (platform-dependent)
gcc-14-base                    Base files common to all compilers
gcc-14-soft-float              Software floating point (ARM only)
gcc-14-source                  The sources with patches

Ada:
libgnat-util14-dev, libgnat-util14   GNAT version library

C:
cpp-14, cpp-14-doc            GNU C Preprocessor
libssp0-dev, libssp0            GCC stack smashing protection library
libquadmath0                    Math routines for the __float128 type
fixincludes                     Fix non-ANSI header files

C, C++ and Fortran 95:
libgomp1-dev, libgomp1		GCC OpenMP (GOMP) support library
libitm1-dev, libitm1		GNU Transactional Memory Library

Biarch support: On some 64-bit platforms which can also run 32-bit code,
Debian provides additional packages containing 32-bit versions of some
libraries.  These packages have names beginning with 'lib32' instead of
'lib', for example lib32stdc++6.  Similarly, on some 32-bit platforms which
can also run 64-bit code, Debian provides additional packages with names
beginning with 'lib64' instead of 'lib'.  These packages contain 64-bit
versions of the libraries.  (At this time, not all platforms and not all
libraries support biarch.)  The license terms for these lib32 or lib64
packages are identical to the ones for the lib packages.

GCC RUNTIME LIBRARY EXCEPTION

Version 3.1, 31 March 2009

Copyright (C) 2009 Free Software Foundation, Inc. <http://fsf.org/>

Everyone is permitted to copy and distribute verbatim copies of this
license document, but changing it is not allowed.

This GCC Runtime Library Exception ("Exception") is an additional
permission under section 7 of the GNU General Public License, version
3 ("GPLv3"). It applies to a given file (the "Runtime Library") that
bears a notice placed by the copyright holder of the file stating that
the file is governed by GPLv3 along with this Exception.

When you use GCC to compile a program, GCC may combine portions of
certain GCC header files and runtime libraries with the compiled
program. The purpose of this Exception is to allow compilation of
non-GPL (including proprietary) programs to use, in this way, the
header files and runtime libraries covered by this Exception.

0. Definitions.

A file is an "Independent Module" if it either requires the Runtime
Library for execution after a Compilation Process, or makes use of an
interface provided by the Runtime Library, but is not otherwise based
on the Runtime Library.

"GCC" means a version of the GNU Compiler Collection, with or without
modifications, governed by version 3 (or a specified later version) of
the GNU General Public License (GPL) with the option of using any
subsequent versions published by the FSF.

"GPL-compatible Software" is software whose conditions of propagation,
modification and use would permit combination with GCC in accord with
the license of GCC.

"Target Code" refers to output from any compiler for a real or virtual
target processor architecture, in executable form or suitable for
input to an assembler, loader, linker and/or execution
phase. Notwithstanding that, Target Code does not include data in any
format that is used as a compiler intermediate representation, or used
for producing a compiler intermediate representation.

The "Compilation Process" transforms code entirely represented in
non-intermediate languages designed for human-written code, and/or in
Java Virtual Machine byte code, into Target Code. Thus, for example,
use of source code generators and preprocessors need not be considered
part of the Compilation Process, since the Compilation Process can be
understood as starting with the output of the generators or
preprocessors.

A Compilation Process is "Eligible" if it is done using GCC, alone or
with other GPL-compatible software, or if it is done without using any
work based on GCC. For example, using non-GPL-compatible Software to
optimize any GCC intermediate representations would not qualify as an
Eligible Compilation Process.

1. Grant of Additional Permission.

You have permission to propagate a work of Target Code formed by
combining the Runtime Library with Independent Modules, even if such
propagation would otherwise violate the terms of GPLv3, provided that
all Target Code was generated by Eligible Compilation Processes. You
may then convey such a combination under terms of your choice,
consistent with the licensing of the Independent Modules.

2. No Weakening of GCC Copyleft.

The availability of this Exception does not imply any general
presumption that third-party software is unaffected by the copyleft
requirements of the license of GCC.

======================================================================
third_party/licenses/libgcc-s1-Debian-copyright.txt
======================================================================

This is the Debian GNU/Linux prepackaged version of the GNU compiler
collection, containing Ada, C, C++, D, Fortran 95, Go, Objective-C,
Objective-C++, and Modula-2 compilers, documentation, and support
libraries.  In addition, Debian provides the gm2 compiler, either in
the same source package, or built from a separate same source package.
Packaging is done by the Debian GCC Maintainers
<debian-gcc@lists.debian.org>, with sources obtained from:

  ftp://gcc.gnu.org/pub/gcc/releases/  (for full releases)
  svn://gcc.gnu.org/svn/gcc/           (for prereleases)
  ftp://sourceware.org/pub/newlib/     (for newlib)
  git://git.savannah.gnu.org/gm2.git   (for Modula-2)

The current gcc-14 source package is taken from the git gcc-14-branch.

Changes: See changelog.Debian.gz

Debian splits the GNU Compiler Collection into packages for each language,
library, and documentation as follows:

Language       Compiler package  Library package    Documentation
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Ada            gnat-14          libgnat-14          gnat-14-doc
C              gcc-14                              gcc-14-doc
C++            g++-14           libstdc++6         libstdc++6-14-doc
D              gdc-14
Fortran 95     gfortran-14      libgfortran5       gfortran-14-doc
Go             gccgo-14         libgo0
Objective C    gobjc-14         libobjc4
Objective C++  gobjc++-14
Modula-2       gm2-14           libgm2
Rust           gccrs-14

For some language run-time libraries, Debian provides source files,
development files, debugging symbols and libraries containing position-
independent code in separate packages:

Language  Sources      Development   Debugging            Position-Independent
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
C++                                  libstdc++6-14-dbg  libstdc++6-14-pic
D         libphobos-14-dev

Additional packages include:

All languages:
libgcc1, libgcc2, libgcc4       GCC intrinsics (platform-dependent)
gcc-14-base                    Base files common to all compilers
gcc-14-soft-float              Software floating point (ARM only)
gcc-14-source                  The sources with patches

Ada:
libgnat-util14-dev, libgnat-util14   GNAT version library

C:
cpp-14, cpp-14-doc            GNU C Preprocessor
libssp0-dev, libssp0            GCC stack smashing protection library
libquadmath0                    Math routines for the __float128 type
fixincludes                     Fix non-ANSI header files

C, C++ and Fortran 95:
libgomp1-dev, libgomp1		GCC OpenMP (GOMP) support library
libitm1-dev, libitm1		GNU Transactional Memory Library

Biarch support: On some 64-bit platforms which can also run 32-bit code,
Debian provides additional packages containing 32-bit versions of some
libraries.  These packages have names beginning with 'lib32' instead of
'lib', for example lib32stdc++6.  Similarly, on some 32-bit platforms which
can also run 64-bit code, Debian provides additional packages with names
beginning with 'lib64' instead of 'lib'.  These packages contain 64-bit
versions of the libraries.  (At this time, not all platforms and not all
libraries support biarch.)  The license terms for these lib32 or lib64
packages are identical to the ones for the lib packages.

GCC RUNTIME LIBRARY EXCEPTION

Version 3.1, 31 March 2009

Copyright (C) 2009 Free Software Foundation, Inc. <http://fsf.org/>

Everyone is permitted to copy and distribute verbatim copies of this
license document, but changing it is not allowed.

This GCC Runtime Library Exception ("Exception") is an additional
permission under section 7 of the GNU General Public License, version
3 ("GPLv3"). It applies to a given file (the "Runtime Library") that
bears a notice placed by the copyright holder of the file stating that
the file is governed by GPLv3 along with this Exception.

When you use GCC to compile a program, GCC may combine portions of
certain GCC header files and runtime libraries with the compiled
program. The purpose of this Exception is to allow compilation of
non-GPL (including proprietary) programs to use, in this way, the
header files and runtime libraries covered by this Exception.

0. Definitions.

A file is an "Independent Module" if it either requires the Runtime
Library for execution after a Compilation Process, or makes use of an
interface provided by the Runtime Library, but is not otherwise based
on the Runtime Library.

"GCC" means a version of the GNU Compiler Collection, with or without
modifications, governed by version 3 (or a specified later version) of
the GNU General Public License (GPL) with the option of using any
subsequent versions published by the FSF.

"GPL-compatible Software" is software whose conditions of propagation,
modification and use would permit combination with GCC in accord with
the license of GCC.

"Target Code" refers to output from any compiler for a real or virtual
target processor architecture, in executable form or suitable for
input to an assembler, loader, linker and/or execution
phase. Notwithstanding that, Target Code does not include data in any
format that is used as a compiler intermediate representation, or used
for producing a compiler intermediate representation.

The "Compilation Process" transforms code entirely represented in
non-intermediate languages designed for human-written code, and/or in
Java Virtual Machine byte code, into Target Code. Thus, for example,
use of source code generators and preprocessors need not be considered
part of the Compilation Process, since the Compilation Process can be
understood as starting with the output of the generators or
preprocessors.

A Compilation Process is "Eligible" if it is done using GCC, alone or
with other GPL-compatible software, or if it is done without using any
work based on GCC. For example, using non-GPL-compatible Software to
optimize any GCC intermediate representations would not qualify as an
Eligible Compilation Process.

1. Grant of Additional Permission.

You have permission to propagate a work of Target Code formed by
combining the Runtime Library with Independent Modules, even if such
propagation would otherwise violate the terms of GPLv3, provided that
all Target Code was generated by Eligible Compilation Processes. You
may then convey such a combination under terms of your choice,
consistent with the licensing of the Independent Modules.

2. No Weakening of GCC Copyleft.

The availability of this Exception does not imply any general
presumption that third-party software is unaffected by the copyleft
requirements of the license of GCC.

third_party/licenses/CodeBrix.WebGpu.Native-THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt

THIRD-PARTY SOFTWARE NOTICES AND INFORMATION

This repository produces three packages: CodeBrix.WebGpu.Native, a thin,
generated .NET binding over the native codebrix_wgpu libraries it P/Invokes
into; CodeBrix.WebGpu.Skia, which shares a GPU device between that binding
and SkiaSharp; and CodeBrix.WebGpu.Graphics, a graphics layer (resources,
pipelines, 2D and 3D renderers, presentation) over the binding. Several things
in this repository and in the packages come from other people; all of them
are covered below.

  1. THE SHIPPED BINARIES. The CodeBrix.WebGpu.Native package's
     runtimes/<rid>/native/ folders contain
     libcodebrix_wgpu.so / libcodebrix_wgpu.dylib / codebrix_wgpu.dll. Each is
     built from the codebrix-wgpu Rust crate in wgpu-native-tools/codebrix-wgpu/
     (written for this repository, MIT), which links wgpu-native, which in turn
     compiles in the wgpu engine crates and their dependencies from crates.io.
     Beside every binary is LICENSE-WgpuNative.txt - composed from
     wgpu-native-tools/licenses/ by wgpu-native-tools/licenses/
     compose-license-wgpunative.sh - with the full licence text of wgpu-native,
     of webgpu-headers and of EVERY crate compiled into the library, grouped by
     licence. That file, identical on every runtime identifier, is the complete
     notice for the binaries; it is not repeated here.

  2. THE VENDORED SOURCE. wgpu-native-tools/wgpu-native/ is an unmodified copy
     of the wgpu-native release (gfx-rs/wgpu-native, tag v29.0.1.1; "wgpu 29.0.3
     via wgpu-native v29.0.1.1"), and wgpu-native-tools/wgpu-native/ffi/
     webgpu-headers/ an unmodified copy of webgpu-native/webgpu-headers at the
     commit that release pins (673658bc2bd70ec39fc55ebe6bb0173cf6d0a603). The
     archives and their SHA-256 sums are in wgpu-native-tools/upstream-downloads/.
     Build-time patches live in wgpu-native-tools/patches/ and are applied to a
     scratch copy only; the vendored trees are never edited.

  3. THE GENERATED BINDING. src/CodeBrix.WebGpu.Native/Generated/*.g.cs is
     generated by tools/CodeBrix.WebGpu.BindingGenerator from:
       - webgpu-headers' webgpu.yml and schema.json (BSD-3-Clause; the API
         description and its documentation text, which becomes the XML
         documentation of the generated members);
       - wgpu-native-tools/specs/wgpu.yml - a transcription, in the
         webgpu-headers schema, of wgpu-native's ffi/wgpu.h (MIT), started from
         the wgpu.yml file of wgpu-native trunk commit
         6f7d734be9bb5d1b3f0f48c9eb3019eec1eaa21a (that file carries
         "Copyright 2019-2023 wgpu-native developers, SPDX-License-Identifier:
         BSD-3-Clause"); its doc text is taken from wgpu.h's comments;
       - wgpu-native-tools/specs/codebrix.yml (this repository, MIT).
     The generator follows the naming and value rules of webgpu-headers'
     reference Go generator (gen/, BSD-3-Clause); no Go code was copied - the
     generator is a new C# program.
     The same generator writes the native-module files
     src/CodeBrix.WebGpu.Native/include/codebrix_wgpu_procs.h and
     codebrix_wgpu_procs.rs from those inputs (the Rust file restates the C
     types of webgpu.h and wgpu.h).

  3a. THE SHIPPED C HEADERS. The CodeBrix.WebGpu.Native package's include/
     folder carries, unmodified, webgpu-headers' webgpu.h (BSD-3-Clause) and
     wgpu-native's ffi/wgpu.h (MIT) from the vendored trees above, beside
     codebrix_wgpu.h (this repository, MIT), the two generated files above and
     a copy of LICENSE-WgpuNative.txt, whose PART 1 (wgpu-native, MIT) and
     PART 2 (webgpu-headers, BSD-3-Clause) are the notices for the two
     headers.

  4. BUILD-TIME TOOLS. The binding generator uses the NuGet packages
     CodeBrix.YamlParse.MitLicenseForever and
     CodeBrix.Templating.BsdLicenseForever. They are tools only: nothing from
     them is compiled into the CodeBrix.WebGpu.Native assembly or shipped in
     its package.

  5. SKIASHARP. CodeBrix.WebGpu.Skia references the SkiaSharp NuGet package
     (mono/SkiaSharp, MIT) as an ordinary package dependency. No SkiaSharp
     source or binary is copied into this repository or into the
     CodeBrix.WebGpu.Skia package; SkiaSharp and its native assets reach an
     application through NuGet under their own licences. CodeBrix.WebGpu.Skia
     is written for this repository (MIT). Its licence text follows (section 4).

  6. CODEBRIX.WEBGPU.GRAPHICS is written for this repository (MIT). It contains
     no third-party code; its WGSL shaders are this repository's own (its
     Radiance .hdr decoder follows the logic of the public-domain stb_image.h
     HDR loader - public domain / MIT-0, no notice required). Besides
     CodeBrix.WebGpu.Native it references two NuGet packages as ordinary
     package dependencies, each reaching an application through NuGet under
     its own licence (nothing of them is copied into this repository or into
     the Graphics package):
       - CodeBrix.Imaging.ApacheLicenseForever (image decoding and encoding;
         Apache License 2.0 - a fork of SixLabors.ImageSharp / Fonts by its
         own repository, ellisnet/CodeBrix.Imaging, which carries its notices);
       - CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2.MitLicenseForever (glTF 2.0 reading; MIT).
     The Graphics package itself stays MIT. Its tests include a few
     public-domain 3D models and an HDRI, listed with their credits in
     section 6 below.

  7. THE SAMPLES. samples/WebGpuModelViewer and samples/WebGpuModelViewer.Android
     (which links the desktop sample's sources and models) are not part of any
     package. They reference the NuGet packages
     CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2.MitLicenseForever, CodeBrix.Sdl3.ZlibLicenseForever,
     SkiaSharp and SkiaSharp.NativeAssets.* (each under its own licence,
     reaching the samples through NuGet), and include a few public-domain 3D
     models, listed with their credits in section 5 below.

  8. THE TEST PROJECTS are not part of any package. Besides the projects of
     this repository they reference xunit.v3, xunit.runner.visualstudio,
     Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk, SilverAssertions.ApacheLicenseForever and
     SkiaSharp.NativeAssets.Linux as NuGet packages (each under its own
     licence) and include the public-domain models and HDRI of section 6.

wgpu-native is offered under "MIT OR Apache-2.0"; this repository uses it under
the MIT License. webgpu-headers is BSD-3-Clause. Both are compatible with this
repository's MIT licence; their texts follow.

Jeremy Ellis and contributors license the CodeBrix.WebGpu project to you under
the terms set forth in the LICENSE file, which is located at the root of this
repository.

believe that any third-party code has been included in CodeBrix.WebGpu in

THIRD-PARTY SOFTWARE NOTICES AND INFORMATION

CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2 is a library for reading, writing and building
Khronos glTF 2.0 3D models (.gltf and .glb) in .NET. It is a port and
adaptation of the SharpGLTF project; the source code of this repository's
library and test projects is derived from SharpGLTF and carries the notice
reproduced in section 1.

The test project additionally carries a small set of 3D model and image files
used as test inputs. Every one of them comes from a source whose license is
identified in section 3 (or was written for this repository); none of them is
part of the CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2 assembly or NuGet package.

Jeremy Ellis and contributors license the CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2 project to
you under the terms set forth in the LICENSE file, which is located at the root
of this repository. The third-party material listed below remains under its own
license, as stated for each item.

If you have any questions about any third-party code or assets referenced here,
or if you believe that any third-party material has been included in

================================================================================
1. SharpGLTF
================================================================================

Project:      SharpGLTF
Source:       https://github.com/vpenades/SharpGLTF
Baseline:     tag v1.0.7, commit acbc151e70d65ceb8bec24fa95f0067d0e5ed933 --
              the source of the SharpGLTF.Core, SharpGLTF.Runtime and
              SharpGLTF.Toolkit 1.0.7 NuGet packages
Copyright:    Copyright (c) 2019 Vicente Penades
              (and the SharpGLTF contributors; see the upstream repository's
              history for the full list)
License:      MIT (full text below)

Scope of the port
-----------------

CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2 incorporates the source code of the three upstream
projects behind the SharpGLTF.Core, SharpGLTF.Runtime and SharpGLTF.Toolkit
NuGet packages, plus the two shared source files each of them links in, merged
into ONE assembly:

  * src/SharpGLTF.Core      -> src/CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2/
                               (glTF 2.0 document model, IO, memory accessors,
                               transforms, animations, validation, reflection)
  * src/SharpGLTF.Runtime   -> src/CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2/Runtime/
                               (scene templates and instances, mesh decoding)
  * src/SharpGLTF.Toolkit   -> src/CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2/
                               (mesh, material and scene builders, vertex
                               types, Schema2 conversion helpers)
  * src/Shared/Guard.cs, src/Shared/_Extensions.cs
                            -> src/CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2/ (root)

The upstream test suites for those projects are likewise incorporated, ported
from NUnit to xUnit.v3 + SilverAssertions, into ONE test project:

  * tests/SharpGLTF.Core.Tests       -> tests/CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2.Tests/
  * tests/SharpGLTF.Runtime.Tests    -> tests/CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2.Tests/Runtime/
  * tests/SharpGLTF.Toolkit.Tests    -> tests/CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2.Tests/
  * tests/SharpGLTF.ThirdParty.Tests -> tests/CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2.Tests/ThirdParty/
  * tests/SharpGLTF.NUnit            -> tests/CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2.Tests/TestSupport/
                                        (test helpers only)

Three small test input files come from the upstream repository's tests/Assets
folder and are covered by the same MIT license:

  * tests/CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2.Tests/Assets/Invalid_Json.gltf
  * tests/CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2.Tests/Assets/white space.gltf
  * tests/CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2.Tests/Assets/SpecialCases/RelativePaths.gltf

tests/CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2.Tests/Assets/API/API.SharpGLTF.1.0.7.txt is a
listing of the public API of the SharpGLTF.Core, SharpGLTF.Runtime and
SharpGLTF.Toolkit 1.0.7 assemblies (namespace renamed), used by a test that
checks this library still exposes every one of those signatures.

Not incorporated: the upstream SharpGLTF.Ext.3DTiles and SharpGLTF.Ext.Agi
extension libraries, the SharpGLTF.CodeGen code generators and the build/
tools, the examples/ projects, the Toolkit's T4 text templates (their generated
.cs output IS incorporated), the AOT and DownloadTestFiles test projects, the
tests that need externally downloaded model collections, and the upstream test
assets whose origin or license could not be identified.

Modifications made during the port
----------------------------------

  * Namespaces renamed: SharpGLTF[.Sub] -> CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2[.Sub].
    Every ported file records its origin with a
    `//was previously: <upstream-namespace>;` comment on its namespace line.
  * The three upstream assemblies were merged into a single assembly and a
    single NuGet package. One file-name collision was resolved by renaming the
    Toolkit's Diagnostics/DebugViews.cs to Diagnostics/DebugViews.Toolkit.cs.
  * Retargeted from the upstream multi-targeting (netstandard2.0,
    netstandard2.1, net6.0, net8.0, net10.0) to net10.0 only. Conditional-
    compilation branches that cannot execute on .NET 10 were removed along
    with their `#if` / `#elif` / `#else` / `#endif` directives; the branch that
    .NET 10 compiles was kept. `#if DEBUG` and the upstream developer toggle
    `SUPRESSTRYCATCH` were kept as-is.
  * Block-scoped namespaces converted to file-scoped namespaces; `using`
    directives that upstream placed inside a namespace block were hoisted above
    it and fully qualified.
  * The glTF `asset.generator` value written into saved models changed from
    "SharpGLTF <version>" to "CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2 <version>".
  * ReadContext.CreateFromDirectory normalises '\' to '/' in relative URIs, so
    models written with Windows path separators load on Linux and macOS too.
  * StyleCop `#pragma` lines removed (the build does not run StyleCop); a few
    malformed XML documentation references and missing <param> tags fixed; the
    three reflection-based diagnostic helpers annotated for trimming analysis.
  * Strong-name signing dropped.
  * Tests: NUnit replaced with xUnit.v3 + SilverAssertions; TestAttachments,
    Plotly.Sharp, Newtonsoft.Json and SixLabors.ImageSharp usage replaced
    (attachments are plain files, plots are CSV files, JSON uses
    System.Text.Json, the one generated PNG uses CodeBrix.Imaging); tests that
    depended on removed or unidentified assets were retargeted to the assets in
    section 3 or dropped.

Code incorporated in SharpGLTF from the .NET runtime

src/CodeBrix.Graphics3D.Gltf2/Transforms/Matrix4x4Double.cs is, per its
upstream comment, stripped from System.Numerics.Matrix4x4 in the .NET runtime
(https://github.com/dotnet/runtime), which is licensed under the MIT License:

    Copyright (c) .NET Foundation and Contributors

    (the MIT License text below applies, with this copyright line)

jxl-oxide 0.12.6 (JPEG XL managed port)
================================================================================

Source: https://github.com/tirr-c/jxl-oxide
Revision: f8ae722ef2d6b782941c89517d19cfbf605c4a9d (tag 0.12.6)
License: Apache-2.0 (selected from MIT OR Apache-2.0)
Author: Wonwoo Choi and jxl-oxide contributors

Adapted into src/CodeBrix.Imaging/Formats/Jxl/Bitstream, Headers, Container,
Coding, Color, Modular, Rendering, and VarDct, plus the spot-color equations in
JxlDecoderCore.Decode.cs. Rendering adaptations include restoration filters,
frame/patch blending, patch bitstream parsing and channel upsampling. Color
adaptations include inverse XYB and YCbCr transforms. Individual source files
identify the upstream source path.
The Vector128 inverse-DCT butterflies in VarDct/JxlDct.Vector.cs derive
from crates/jxl-render/src/vardct/x86_64/dct/mod.rs at the same revision;
the managed vector path preserves the scalar path's row-first operation order.
The C# port supplies stream integration, validation and inverse field writers.
Encoder/Modular/JxlModularEncoder.cs uses the inverse grammar, reversible color
transform and clamped-gradient equations of those attributed managed Modular
sources. Its entropy writers separately retain the libjxl attribution below.
Encoder/Modular/JxlRctEncoder.cs inverts transform/rct.rs for all 42 reversible
color transforms. Encoder/VarDct/JxlForwardTransform.cs inverts the attributed
decoder transforms and shares its AFV basis and DCT normalization tables.
Encoder/VarDct/JxlVarDctEncoder.cs inverts the attributed frame, HF metadata
and coefficient token grammar and uses the shared managed entropy writers.
JxlPaletteEncoder.cs inverts transform/palette.rs for exact
explicit palettes. Color/JxlIccCodec.Encode.cs inverts the ICC header, tag and
command grammar from crates/jxl-color/src/icc/decode.rs. Container box writers
invert the attributed container reader. Their selection/buffering integration
is specific to CodeBrix.Imaging; entropy primitives are attributed separately.
JpegReconstruction/JxlJpegData.Write.cs inverts the fields and Huffman table
grammar in crates/jxl-jbr/src/lib.rs and huffman.rs at the same revision, using
BCL Brotli for the byte payload.

src/CodeBrix.Imaging/Formats/Jxl/Coding/JxlAnsHistogram.cs adapts the alias-table
algorithm through jxl-oxide 0.12.6 crates/jxl-coding/src/ans.rs (revision recorded
above). That upstream file explicitly identifies its libjxl derivation but does
not identify the historical libjxl revision. The alias-table algorithm was also
reviewed in lib/jxl/ans_common.cc at the audited revision above. The C# adaptation
uses portable managed structures. Jeremy Ellis and contributors' modifications are Apache-2.0.
src/CodeBrix.Imaging/Formats/Jxl/VarDct/JxlLfGlobal.cs checks context limits
against lib/jxl/entropy_coder.cc at the libjxl revision recorded above.
src/CodeBrix.Imaging/Formats/Jxl/JxlDecoderCore.Decode.cs uses the rendering
stage order from lib/jxl/dec_cache.cc at that revision: noise is added after
upsampling, while patches and splines are applied before color upsampling.
Its skipped-preview noise indexing follows lib/jxl/dec_frame.cc: the preview
counts as an invisible frame for references before the first displayed frame.

src/CodeBrix.Imaging/Formats/Jxl/Encoder/Entropy/JxlPrefixEncoder.cs adapts
lib/jxl/enc_huffman.cc and lib/jxl/enc_huffman_tree.cc at that revision:
length-limited Huffman trees, canonical codes and run-length-coded tree storage.
The managed implementation uses 64-bit histogram sums to avoid count overflow.
Encoder/Entropy/JxlAnsEncoder*.cs adapts the ANS histogram normalization,
precision search, histogram serialization and symbol coder in lib/jxl/enc_ans.cc,
enc_ans.h and ans_common.h at the same revision. It inverts the shared managed
alias table for encoding. Managed histogram cost estimates use double-precision
logarithms; the normalization step retains upstream fixed-point entropy deltas.
The managed normalizer explicitly prevents used bins from shrinking below one
state while repairing an initially nonpositive balancing bin after rounding.
Encoder/Entropy/JxlLz77.cs adapts token cost estimation, hash-chain matching,
repeat parsing and dynamic-programming refinement from lib/jxl/enc_lz77.cc at
the same revision. Managed changes include absolute chain positions, effort
dependent search limits, double-precision cost estimates, long-periodic-run
bounds and final selection by actual encoded bit count. The special-distance
table is shared with the jxl-oxide-derived managed decoder.
Greedy rejected-match skipping follows ApplyLZ77_LZ77 in enc_lz77.cc;
managed chain comparisons are additionally limited to 65,536 samples per
candidate. Both bounds prevent repeated scans of cheaply coded periodic input.
Encoder/Entropy/JxlHistogramOptimizer.cs adapts versioned priority-queue
histogram merging and the prefix single-symbol merge penalty from
lib/jxl/enc_cluster.cc, and hybrid-integer candidate configurations and their
selection from enc_ans.cc at that revision. Managed merge ranking uses bounded
histograms and double-precision estimates; final selection compares complete
encoded bit counts, including configuration and context-map overhead.
Eight-byte token storage, zero-copy traversal of grouped token arrays in
JxlTokenSequence.cs, and bounded distinct-value collection for configuration
selection are original managed changes by Jeremy Ellis and contributors.
After 65,536 distinct values, configuration selection accumulates the same
candidate histograms directly, preserving exhaustive candidate costs.
Encoder/JxlEncoderPreflight.cs is original managed admission control for
encoder working-memory estimates and frame-section limits. Its estimates cover
managed tokens, retained candidate streams, imported planes, raw features and
metadata; it uses the separately attributed frame geometry without altering
the requested coding tools. Encoder workspace exception classification and
early JPEG coefficient-allocation checks are original integration changes.
Encoder/Entropy/JxlEntropyEncoder.cs adapts context-map move-to-front,
entropy and run-length candidate selection from lib/jxl/enc_context_map.cc
and enc_ans_params.h at the same revision. The managed writer compares actual
bit counts for simple, prefix, ANS and run-length representations, with bounded
recursion for the two-context run-length model's own context map.
For more than 256 input contexts, distant-seed selection and nearest-cluster
assignment follow FastClusterHistograms in enc_cluster.cc before pair merging.
All input distributions are retained until clustering; context-index modulo
grouping is only a baseline candidate, never the input to the optimized search.
Encoder/Entropy/JxlPermutationEncoder.cs adapts Lehmer-rank tokenization from
lib/jxl/enc_coeff_order.cc at the same revision, using a managed Fenwick tree
for bounded O(n log n) work. Headers/JxlFrameToc.cs uses it for reordered TOCs.
Encoder/VarDct/JxlXybEncoder.cs adapts the linear-sRGB-to-XYB absorbance matrix,
intensity scaling and cube-root transform from lib/jxl/enc_xyb.cc and
cms/opsin_params.h at that revision, using BCL floating-point operations.
Its raw-header path inverts the caller's rounded custom opsin matrix and
biases using the managed matrix routines. Preview frame geometry follows
lib/jxl/frame_header.cc: omitted preview dimensions refer to the preview
canvas, independently of the main image dimensions.
VarDct/JxlDequantMatrices.Encode.cs inverts the attributed jxl-oxide raw
matrix grammar. The public transform/matrix API, power-of-two quantization
and propagation through strategy, chroma prediction, quantization and
perceptual reconstruction are original managed integration. Raw rectangular
matrix wire dimensions in both reader and writer are corrected against
libjxl quant_weights.h, dec_modular.cc and enc_modular.cc at the same revision;
the Modular image is narrow/tall, and its flattened coefficient layout is
wide/short. Default and parametrized matrix generation retain their original
jxl-oxide provenance.
Encoder/VarDct/JxlNoiseEstimator.cs adapts flat-patch SAD selection,
Laplacian noise measurements, asymmetric regularized LUT fitting and the
scaled conjugate-gradient solver from lib/jxl/enc_noise.cc, enc_optimize.h,
noise.h and enc_frame.cc at the same revision. The managed version bounds
fitting to forty iterations, checks cancellation, guards zero gradients and
empty samples, and quantizes the final LUT before writing. Estimation is
explicitly enabled through NoiseModeling; the default matches the pinned
reference's disabled estimation throughout the supported distance range.
Encoder/VarDct/JxlLossyPatchEncoder.cs adapts text-like flat-background seeds,
nearby background growth, connected components, perceptual duplicate keys and
additive reference-frame organization from lib/jxl/enc_patch_dictionary.cc.
Its distance-dependent, non-progressive Modular XYB atlas precision follows
enc_modular.cc; dequantizers are rounded through binary16 before sample
quantization, following enc_quant_weights.cc at the same revision.
Managed differences include one bounded pixel queue, compact background seed
indices, bounded hash buckets/candidate storage, shelf atlas packing, and a
Modular atlas whose decoded samples are also used for subtraction
and perceptual evaluation. This text-patch search is separate from dot search.
JxlLossyPatchEncoder.Dots.cs adapts the two Gaussian guidance filters,
component energy/score thresholds, moment fitting, least-squares intensities
and dot acceptance from lib/jxl/enc_detect_dots.cc and enc_dot_dictionary.cc.
The managed implementation uses a closed-form symmetric 2x2 covariance
eigendecomposition, bounds retained components to one hundred, and fully
visits rejected large components instead of restarting their search.
Encoder/VarDct/JxlVarDctPreparation.cs adapts initial DC/AC quantization,
global scale selection, dead zones and reconstructed-luma prediction from
lib/jxl/enc_heuristics.cc, enc_adaptive_quantization.cc, quantizer.cc and
enc_group.cc at that revision. LF extraction inverts the attributed managed
jxl-oxide reconstruction. JxlEncoder.cs uses the quality-to-distance mapping
from JxlEncoderDistanceFromQuality in lib/jxl/encode.cc at that revision.
Its positive-distance floor follows JxlEncoderSetFrameDistance and the
kMinButteraugliDistance constant in enc_params.h at that revision.
Encoder/VarDct/JxlVarDctInput.cs is original integration of the attributed
managed ICC, enumerated-color and XYB components with CodeBrix pixel import.
Encoder/VarDct/JxlVarDctEncoder.cs also adapts the three AC frequency passes
from lib/jxl/enc_frame.cc and enc_progressive_split.cc at that revision,
with shared frame headers and a separate entropy model for each pass.
Its default edge-preserving filter iteration thresholds follow enc_frame.cc;
the initial sharpness of four follows enc_heuristics.cc. Low-frequency
smoothing is enabled by default, using the shared frame flag when disabled.
Its no-Gaborish initial quantization distance adjustment also follows
enc_heuristics.cc at that revision.
Encoder/VarDct/JxlCoefficientOrder.cs adapts zero-frequency sorting, natural
order tie-breaking, quantized counts and the size limits from enc_coeff_order.cc
at that revision. It counts all eligible blocks and shares the existing
Lehmer permutation writer; native sampling/dispatch machinery is not copied.
Encoder/VarDct/JxlChromaFromLuma.cs adapts the initial 8x8 and final selected-
transform, quantization-weighted color-correlation searches from
lib/jxl/enc_chroma_from_luma.cc at that revision: regularized least squares,
the bounded Newton search, its shared residual outlier mask for approximate
curvature, soft threshold and signed-byte range. Managed scalar accumulation
uses double precision and bounded 64x64 tile scratch. JxlChromaFromLumaTests
includes native SSE2 multiplier results from the same pinned source for
original deterministic CodeBrix samples spanning the outlier threshold.
Encoder/VarDct/JxlPhotonNoise.cs adapts the sensor/ISO noise model and LUT
quantization from lib/jxl/enc_photon_noise.cc and enc_noise.cc at that revision,
using double intermediates to keep all finite positive ISO values bounded.
Encoder/VarDct/JxlChromaticityQuantization.cs adapts the distance thresholds,
worst neighboring XYB differences and exposed-blue measurements from
PixelStatsForChromacityAdjustment and ComputeChromacityAdjustments in
lib/jxl/enc_frame.cc at that revision. It examines the edge-extended block
rectangle without allocating padding and checks cancellation per row.
The test fixture JxlSynthetic/encoder-transform-reference.bin contains scalar
forward-transform results generated by this pinned libjxl implementation from
an original deterministic CodeBrix sample pattern. Its adjacent text file
records the generator inputs, binary layout and SHA-256. The fixture provides
an independent numerical reference; the tests do not load a native library.
Encoder/VarDct/JxlInverseGabor.cs adapts the approximate inverse Gaborish kernel
and symmetric five-tap-per-axis convolution from lib/jxl/enc_gaborish.cc and
convolve.h at that revision. It uses one allocator-backed scratch plane and
the attributed managed mirrored boundary helper. Enablement follows
enc_frame.cc: effort five or greater and perceptual distance above 0.5.
Encoder/VarDct/JxlAdaptiveQuantization.cs adapts the initial quantization field
from enc_adaptive_quantization.cc at that revision: gamma-adjusted local
differences, fuzzy erosion, masking, gamma/high-frequency/blue modulations and
distance dampening. It uses managed allocator-backed grids and BCL log/exp
functions. The fine strategy mask uses the attributed logarithmic Laplacian
and symmetric 5x5 blur. Butteraugli iterations are not included in this
initial component.
Encoder/VarDct/JxlAcStrategy.cs adapts transform entropy/error estimation,
distance/effort-dependent transform costs, and rectangular/square split/merge
search from lib/jxl/enc_ac_strategy.cc and quant_weights.cc at that revision.
The managed search uses bounded 64x64 tile scratch and cached estimates,
double-precision cost accumulation, and explicit overlap checks. Its edge
search follows hierarchical merges rather than the native priority scan.
Encoder/VarDct/JxlAcQuantizer.cs adapts per-block quantizer refinement and
frequency-quadrant dead zones from lib/jxl/enc_group.cc at that revision:
low-activity boundaries, isolated high-frequency detail, large-transform
error and texture activity. Managed cost accumulation uses double precision
and clamps before integer conversion. The upstream error_diffusion parameter
is unused by that revision's QuantizeBlockAC implementation.
Encoder/VarDct/JxlBlockContextModel.cs adapts transform-order/quantizer frequency
counts, quantizer thresholds and low-count cluster merging from
FindBestBlockEntropyModel in enc_heuristics.cc, with defaults from
entropy_coder.cc at that revision. Managed counting weights transform anchors
by their covered area and uses final quantizers, with deterministic tie breaks.
Encoder/Butteraugli/ ports the perceptual comparator, opsin dynamics, frequency
decomposition, directional Malta filters, asymmetric error accumulation,
activity masking, half-resolution comparison and small-image padding from
lib/jxl/butteraugli/butteraugli.cc at that revision. The blur's mirrored 5-tap
case follows enc_convolve_separable5.cc; the gamma approximation follows
base/fast_math-inl.h and base/rational_polynomial-inl.h. Managed code uses
allocator-owned planes, cancellation checks, BCL scalar math and explicit
fused multiply-add where the reference uses it. The unused deeper recursive
reference pyramid is omitted; both resolutions used by the comparator remain.
The row lookup and bounded vertical-tile optimization in the blur is original
managed work and retains the same floating-point operation order. Its previous
scalar implementation is retained in JxlButteraugliBlurTests as a bit-exact
regression reference under the same source attribution.
Encoder/VarDct/JxlPerceptualQuantizer.cs adapts FindBestQuantization,
AdjustQuantField and TileDistMap from enc_adaptive_quantization.cc at that
revision: fixed-transform quantization trials, sixteenth-norm block errors,
bounded field updates and two/four refinement rounds at efforts eight/nine.
It preserves the initial selected-transform color-correlation maps throughout
refinement, following the search ordering in enc_heuristics.cc at that revision.
It uses the separately attributed managed Butteraugli and decoder components.
Tile errors use normalized double accumulation to avoid HDR overflow.
JxlVarDctPreparation's iterative global scale uses the median and median
absolute deviation from quantizer.cc. JxlVarDctRoundtrip.cs is original
integration that reuses the managed decoder's transforms and restoration
without repeating entropy coding; synthesized noise is excluded from the
search, as in the reference RoundtripImage pipeline.
The FasterDecoding settings in JxlVarDctEncoder, JxlAcStrategy and
JxlBlockContextModel follow enc_frame.cc, enc_ac_strategy.cc and
enc_heuristics.cc at that revision: filter reductions, transform-size limits,
the simple two-class block map and six AC histograms. Modular restrictions
in JxlModularSearchOptions follow enc_modular.cc, enc_frame.cc and enc_ans.cc:
omit weighted prediction, use 128-pixel groups, restrict gradient prediction
and disable MA learning at the highest setting, with twelve histograms from
setting two. The entropy optimizer applies the cap to both candidates and
their fallback distributions. These constraints also apply to expert search
candidates, chunked frames, patch references and VarDCT's Modular streams.
Encoder/VarDct/JxlDownsampling.cs adapts DownsampleImage2_Sharper,
DownsampleImage2_Iterative, CreateMask and AntiUpsample from enc_heuristics.cc,
and box averaging from image_ops.cc at that revision. It retains the symmetric
12x12 filter, ringing bounds, three derivative-based refinement rounds at
effort ten and box sampling for factors four/eight and extra channels.
The managed version omits unused perceptual-mask allocations and initializes
maxima to negative infinity so negative samples have correct clipping bounds.
Encoder dispatch and the resampled Butteraugli-search threshold follow
enc_frame.cc and enc_adaptive_quantization.cc at that revision.
Encoder/Modular/JxlLossyModularEncoder.cs adapts the XYB scale factors,
YX(B-Y) channel order, per-component/per-resolution Squeeze quantizers,
signed rounding and global/LF/HF stream organization from enc_modular.cc
and enc_frame.cc at that revision. Extra-channel quantization remains one
for exact alpha. JxlSqueezeEncoder's default layout follows the attributed
managed decoder grammar and libjxl modular/transform/squeeze.cc and squeeze_params.cc;
component identities are retained across transforms for quantizer selection.
VarDct/JxlDequantMatrices.Defaults.cs corrects the default 128x256 and 256x128
dequantization weights against lib/jxl/quant_weights.cc at the same revision.
The inherited oxide Y and B constants differed from the reference decoder.
Encoder/Modular/FastLossless/ adapts the dedicated effort-1 path from
lib/jxl/enc_fast_lossless.cc at that revision: fixed per-channel gradient tree,
sampled shared two-level prefix tables, per-symbol length limits, YCoCg and
eight-sample zero-run coding. The managed implementation imports bounded
256-pixel groups and uses the shared header/TOC and prefix-length writers.
The native SIMD, C ABI and output-buffer alignment machinery are not copied.
Encoder/Modular/JxlPaletteEncoder.cs additionally adapts the implicit color
cubes, retention of frequent implicit colors, image-order candidates and
frequency/luma/alpha ordering from modular/transform/enc_palette.cc at that
revision. Lossless candidates are selected by their complete encoded size.
Modular/JxlPaletteTransform.cs corrects implicit extra-channel values to zero
as specified by modular/transform/palette.h at that revision; this differs
from the originally ported jxl-oxide calculation for the small color cube.
Encoder/Modular/JxlModularSearchOptions.cs ports the two expert-effort probes
and the 24/20 conditional configuration lists from lib/jxl/enc_frame.cc
(TectonicPlateSettingsLessPalette/MorePalette) at that revision. Managed
orchestration compares complete frame bytes, preserves the ordinary effort-10
candidate and deduplicates identical configurations. Sampling, predictor and
weighted-tree restrictions follow modular/encoding/enc_ma.cc; deterministic
sample selection and bounded managed tree learning remain port adaptations.
JxlRctEncoder.cs uses the effort-dependent 4/5/7/9/19 candidate sequence from
lib/jxl/enc_modular.cc at that revision. All 42 wire transforms remain supported.
JxlMaEncoder.cs serializes residual multipliers using enc_ma.cc's trailing-zero
exponent/odd-part grammar. The exact greatest-common-divisor refinement over
all encoded residual streams is original managed integration; a multiplier is
never inferred solely from the MA learning sample.
Encoder/Modular/JxlMaEncoder.cs adapts entropy-based predictor selection and
property-threshold tree splitting from lib/jxl/modular/encoding/enc_ma.cc at
the same revision. Managed changes include bounded deterministic sampling,
sorted threshold sweeps, double-precision entropy estimates and median residual
offset candidates. It shares the decoder's exact predictors and properties.
Fixed gradient/WP trees and their pixel-count/precision-scaled thresholds follow
MakeFixedTree and PredefinedTree in modular/encoding/enc_encoding.cc at that pin.
Encoder/Modular/JxlSqueezeEncoder.cs adapts forward horizontal/vertical squeeze
from lib/jxl/modular/transform/enc_squeeze.cc at that revision. It uses explicit
managed plane ownership, shares the attributed decoder's tendency equation and
selects a candidate only when its complete encoded stream is smaller.
Encoder/Modular/JxlWeightedPredictorEncoder.cs adapts the five predictor presets
in lib/jxl/modular/encoding/context_predict.h and the WP-error-conditioned
histogram cost selection in lib/jxl/enc_modular.cc at the same revision. It
uses double-precision entropy estimates and the shared managed predictor state.
Encoder/Modular/JxlModularEncoder.GlobalTree.cs follows global MA-tree and
shared histogram organization in lib/jxl/enc_modular.cc and
lib/jxl/modular/encoding/enc_encoding.cc at that revision. Its managed candidates
retain independent group entropy/LZ77 states and compare complete payload sizes.
Encoder/Modular/JxlModularEncoder.Chunked.cs follows LF-group-sized input
chunking and lossless eligibility in lib/jxl/enc_frame.cc at the same revision.
The managed path releases sample planes after each chunk and retains compressed
payloads to support forward-only output without temporary files.
Rendering/JxlPatches.Encode.cs adapts patch tokenization from
lib/jxl/enc_patch_dictionary.cc at the same revision. The alpha-selection
condition in JxlPatches.cs follows dec_patch_dictionary.cc: explicit selection
is present when there is more than one extra channel, regardless of its type.
Rendering/JxlSplines.Encode.cs adapts spline token contexts, starting-point
deltas and coefficient serialization from lib/jxl/enc_splines.cc at that pin.
Its validation and second-difference construction integrate the attributed
managed spline decoder. JxlRawImage, JxlRawFrameEncoding, JxlRawEncoder and
Encoder/JxlFrameFeatures are original public API, ownership and integration
code around the separately attributed field and feature writers.
Encoder/VarDct/JxlLowFrequencyEncoder.cs follows the separate Modular LF-frame
organization, placeholder extra channels, and pre-color-transform reference
handling in lib/jxl/enc_cache.cc and enc_frame.cc at the same libjxl revision.
The power-of-two representation is original; LF smoothing and reconstruction
reuse the separately attributed managed decoder. Progressive Modular output
uses the existing attributed Squeeze layout and pass-group selection grammar.
JxlPatches.cs and JxlCompositor.cs follow color/alpha precedence and background
alpha reference selection in lib/jxl/blending.cc, alpha.cc and
render_pipeline/stage_blending.cc at that pin. Color alpha blending writes its
resulting alpha even when that extra channel has a separate blending mode.
Headers/JxlFrameHeader.cs follows per-channel blending-source field presence in
lib/jxl/frame_header.cc: an extra channel's own mode determines whether its
reference source is serialized, independently of the color channels' mode.
Its progressive-pass validation also follows Passes::VisitFields in that
pinned frame_header.cc: decreasing downsampling, increasing last-pass indices,
and indices bounded by the pass count. Equal downsample and pass counts are
allowed, matching the reference implementation.
Encoder/Modular/JxlLosslessPatchEncoder.cs follows the reference-frame atlas
organization in lib/jxl/enc_patch_dictionary.cc at that pin. Its managed exact
tile hash search verifies collisions and compares complete encoded candidates;
it does not implement the upstream perceptual/text-component detection.
Encoder/Jpeg/JxlJpegParser*.cs and JxlJpegInputBits.cs adapt JPEG marker,
Huffman, sequential/progressive coefficient and restart parsing from
lib/jxl/jpeg/enc_jpeg_data_reader.cc, plus metadata classification and color
selection from enc_jpeg_data.cc at the same revision. Managed changes use
bounded span reads, pooled coefficient planes, explicit disposal and a scalar
canonical Huffman reader without speculative byte reads.
The reconstruction preflight checks, scan-count preflight before pixel fallback,
caller-configurable resource budgets, bounded output adapter, and incremental
Brotli payload reader are original CodeBrix changes. Final DC representability
is checked after progressive refinement against the separately attributed JPEG
XL reconstruction clamp. Huffman all-ones rejection was checked against the
same pinned enc_jpeg_data_reader.cc; the existing JPEG decoder keeps its
Apache-2.0 provenance and its equivalent rejection.
Encoder/Jpeg/JxlJpegEncoder.cs adapts JPEG coefficient preparation, quantization
scaling and channel ordering from lib/jxl/enc_frame.cc at the same revision.
Its field and coefficient token writers invert the attributed managed VarDCT
decoder grammar; it shares its frequency/nonzero context tables and natural
coefficient order. Managed changes use pooled planes and owned section buffers.
JPEG reconstruction also follows lib/jxl/jpeg/jpeg_data.cc at that revision
for nine-bit Huffman sentinels, empty DHT markers and quantization-table indexes.

src/CodeBrix.Imaging/Formats/Jxl/Color/JxlSampleConverter.cs also adapts the
int_to_float routine in lib/jxl/dec_modular.cc at the audited revision, including
subnormal, signed-zero, infinity and NaN handling for custom float precisions.
The upstream notices and patent grant are retained here in full.

Rendering/JxlSplines.cs and JxlSplines.Encode.cs use the spline/control-point
count limits and cumulative starting-point accounting from lib/jxl/splines.cc
at this same revision. VarDct/JxlHfMetadata.cs follows lib/jxl/dec_modular.cc
for the prohibition on transforms spanning multiple 8x8 blocks when chroma
channels are subsampled; transforms confined to one block remain supported.
Extension payload buffering, Modular channel lookup and decoder patch-work
accounting are original managed resource-management changes.

Encoder/Modular/JxlModularEncoder.PaletteSearch.cs adapts scalar EstimateCost
from lib/jxl/enc_modular_simd.cc and the estimated palette selection strategy
from lib/jxl/enc_modular.cc at the same pin. The managed version samples at most
16,384 positions per channel, ranks whole-frame candidates before group encoding,
and compares selected palette streams against actual untransformed output size.
Efforts 10/11 retain exhaustive whole-frame palette comparisons. The bounded,
sample-verified Modular encoding cache is original managed optimization work.

ICC transport preflight follows the encoded-profile cap in lib/jxl/icc_codec.cc,
its decoded-size-plus-65536 command-expansion limit, and the 4 MiB Level 5 ICC
limit in lib/jxl/encode.cc at that pin. Literal-command fallback and bounded
forward prefix entropy writing for large ICC payloads are original managed
adaptations of the attributed command/entropy grammars.

================================================================================
skcms (managed ICC color-management adaptation)
================================================================================

Source: https://skia.googlesource.com/skcms
Audited reference revision: 7e572ada698a60ff50bd9038fd6e01e44f40868a
License: BSD-3-Clause.

src/CodeBrix.Imaging/ColorSpaces/Icc/IccData.cs, IccCurve.cs, IccLut.cs and
IccColorProfile.cs adapt
bounded ICC reading, profile/PCS conversion, curve evaluation, A2B/B2A LUT
parsing and multidimensional
CLUT interpolation from skcms.cc and
src/Transform_inl.h at the revision above. The implementation uses managed C#
and .NET math, with direct inversion of monotone tables. Jeremy Ellis and
contributors' modifications are Apache-2.0. Original corrections to IccLut.cs
apply PCSXYZ scaling at the LUT boundary, preserve legacy lut16Type PCSLAB
encoding, and apply/clamp legacy XYZ input matrices. These follow the numerical
encodings and processing order in ICC.1:2022 sections 6.3.4.2 and 10.10-10.13
(https://www.color.org/specification/ICC.1-2022-05.pdf), not source code from
another color engine. Generated numerical regressions cover these corrections;
the original nonlinear LUT fixtures are compared with their defining polynomial
because the pinned skcms reference folds XYZ scaling into the wrong stage.
The CMYK fixture's native A2B reference is adjusted only for the legacy Lab
endpoint encoding that skcms omits; its native interpolation samples are retained.
The complete upstream skcms notice follows.
